A major incident has been declared as firefighters battle a large heathland fire at Dunwich Heath near Leiston, about 3 miles from Sizewell B.

items.title: Europe burns: a visual guide to the wildfires
items.summary_raw:
Ferocious flames continue to rage in parts of France and Spain, with no sign of abating. We chart the destruction in graphics and pictures

The hellish infernos that have torn through parts of France and Spain have caused deaths, the evacuation of 330,000 people from their homes, widespread destruction and clouds of toxic smoke. Records have already been smashed and with the fourth heatwave of the European summer setting in, there are few signs of the waves of wildfires ending.

France has already surpassed the worst previous year for the size of the area burned, with August, usually the hottest month, yet to come.

items.summary_raw: Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta is facing a humanitarian and security emergency after about 1,500 migrants swam across from Morocco in the past week.  Ceuta's leader, Juan Jesus Vivas, said reception centers are overwhelmed, with hundreds sleeping outdoors and facilities for unaccompanied minors operating at 2,400% capacity.   Arrivals are averaging 300 people a day, raising fears of a repeat of the 2021 crisis, when around 10,000 migrants entered Ceuta within days.

items.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this summer, official data shows
items.summary_raw:
UKHSA estimates 2,877 fatalities during heatwaves in May and June, almost twice that recorded in 2025 season

England is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths this summer after the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves.

The record was set in 2022 with 2,985 deaths, and August, traditionally the hottest month, is yet to arrive. The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves.”

items.title: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships
items.summary_raw:
Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships

Egypt has attributed a fire that damaged two vessels at the Mediterranean port of Damietta to a drone attack, marking its first official account of Wednesday’s incident.

The Egyptian cabinet said preliminary findings showed that a drone caused the 29 July blaze. No group has taken responsibility.

Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of the attack, citing the need to defend Egypt’s national security and interests.

Maritime security company Ambrey said the drone struck a US-owned floating gas storage tanker before flames spread to a second vessel. Officials reported no casualties.

Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry had previously confirmed the fire but did not identify its cause.

items.title: US munition stockpile could impact operations in Iran, senior army leader tells Trump
items.summary_raw:
US munition stockpile could impact operations in Iran, senior army leader tells Trump

The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine told US President Donald Trump that the situation regarding munitions stockpile could impact military operations in Iran, AP reported citing a US official.

A recent analysis by Washington think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies suggested that the latest war on Iran has drained more of the US army's already diminished stockpiles of Patriot and THAAD interceptors.

The analysis piece suggested that this would put American troops at more risk if the conflict in the region continues.
items.summary_el: Ο προϊστάμενος της Σύνδεσης Αρχηγών Γενικών Επιτελών των ΗΠΑ Dan Caine προειδοποίησε τον Πρόεδρο Trump ότι τα τρέχοντα αποθέματα πυρομachικών θα μπορούσαν να περιορίσουν τις στρατιωτικές επιχειρήσεις κατά του Ιράν.

items.summary_raw: Visioner ‼️🇺🇸🇪🇬💥 A U.S.-owned LNG floating storage facility was reportedly struck by a drone while moored at Egypt's Damietta Port, marking another security incident affecting critical energy infrastructure in the Eastern Mediterranean.  According to maritime security firm Ambrey, the Marshall Islands-flagged, U.S.-owned floating LNG storage facility was hit by at least one drone while docked at Damietta Port.  🔹 No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, while initial reports indicate no casualties and no damage to the port's infrastructure.  📍 The vessel was reportedly the only target affected during the incident, with port operations remaining intact.  Although the physical damage appears to have been limited, the incident underscores the growing vulnerability of strategic energy assets as regional tensions escalate. A successful strike against an LNG facility, even without significant destruction, sends a message that commercial energy infrastructure is increasingly being drawn into the broader confrontation, raising concerns for maritime security and global energy supply routes. Three Greek firefighters have died while tackling wildfires on the island of Crete and in the south of the mainland, the Greek fire department has said, as extreme heat hinders efforts to control blazes ravaging southern Europe.

items.title: Trump and Netanyahu explored all Iran options including attack, Israeli official says
items.summary_raw:
Trump and Netanyahu explored all Iran options including attack, Israeli official says

US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu explored all paths to curb Iran's nuclear project in their meeting this week, including diplomacy, economic pressure and military force, a senior Israeli official said on Wednesday.

Netanyahu did not tell Trump that Israel's preference was for an attack on Iran, the official said in a briefing with reporters on Tuesday.

"In the end, it's his decision," the official said of Trump. Trump has three options, and all three were discussed at length, the official said: "A deal, continuing the blockade and economic pressures, and a massive strike."

Via @Israel_Alma_org

items.title: CSIS estimates the US has burned through so much of its air defense stockpile in the Iran war that Patriot inventories are now under 1,000 interceptors and THAAD is down to about 2…
items.summary_raw: CSIS estimates the US has burned through so much of its air defense stockpile in the Iran war that Patriot inventories are now under 1,000 interceptors and THAAD is down to about 250.  Pre-war baselines were roughly 2,330 Patriots and 360 THAADs, meaning more than half of each has been used up.  On top of that, more than 1,000 Tomahawks and 1,100 JASSMs have been fired, along with heavy drawdowns of SM-3, SM-6, and PrSM missiles.  Rebuild timelines are brutal.  Tomahawk, THAAD, and Patriot need 3+ years to return to pre-war levels, with major FY27 Patriot buys not delivering until May 2029.  It leaves a multi-year vulnerability window for any Western Pacific fight with China.  It also constrains transfers to Ukraine and Gulf allies.

items.title: Visioner 🇺🇦🇺🇸🛡️ President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to U.S. President Donald Trump for an emergency “winter package” of Patriot interceptor missiles, warning that Ukraine’s a…
items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇦🇺🇸🛡️ President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to U.S. President Donald Trump for an emergency “winter package” of Patriot interceptor missiles, warning that Ukraine’s air defense stockpiles are nearing exhaustion ahead of the cold season. items.title: Paros: Next Hours Critical for Full Control of Wildfire, Deputy Mayor Says
items.summary_raw:
PAROS, Greece - The firefighting operation on the Greek island of Paros continued on July 29 with ground forces and two helicopters deployed, as crews battled repeated flare-ups caused by strong winds. According to Charilaos Giourtzidis, deputy mayor for Civil Protection of the Municipality of Paros, wind speeds in the area were as high as 8 Beaufort. Speaking to the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (ANA-MPA), Giourtzidis said ground firefighting forces were currently operating at the scene, supported by two helicopters carrying out continuous water drops. He noted that, despite the challenging weather conditions, the wildfire situation was improved and almost all fronts were showing signs of dying down. However, authorities remain on high alert, as strong winds could trigger new outbreaks or rekindle existing hotspots at any moment.

The post Paros: Next Hours Critical for Full Control of Wildfire, Deputy Mayor Says appeared first on The National Herald.

NICOSIA — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced that a new expanded 5+1 meeting on the Cyprus issue will be convened following sufficient preparations on confidence-building measures, methodology, and substantive content, taking into account the convergences already achieved. Speaking after the joint meeting with President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman in the United Nations buffer zone at Nicosia airport, Guterres said he has the agreement of both sides and the guarantor powers to proceed with a new 5+1 meeting, provided that adequate preparation is undertaken regarding confidence-building, methodology, and substance.

The post UN Secretary-General Guterres Announces New 5+1 Expanded Meeting on Cyprus appeared first on The National Herald.

items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇱🇹🚨🇧🇾 Lithuanian authorities have uncovered an underground tunnel being dug from Belarus toward the Lithuanian border, in what is believed to be another attempt to facilitate illegal cross-border activity.  According to LRT, border guards in southeastern Lithuania detected unusual ground vibrations, raising suspicions that an underground passage was being excavated from the Belarusian side.  🔹 Lithuanian officials requested assistance from Polish specialists equipped with underground detection technology. After drilling a test shaft, they discovered a tunnel approximately one meter in diameter at a depth of around 1.5 meters. The passage had not yet reached the Lithuanian side.  📍 Border authorities believe the tunnel was intended to smuggle illegal migrants, noting that similar underground routes originating from Belarus have previously been uncovered in both Lithuania and Poland, where they were used for transporting people and contraband.  The discovery highlights the increasingly sophisticated methods being employed along NATO's eastern frontier. items.title: Ships stuck in strait of Hormuz pose ‘super-spreader’ biodiversity threat, scientists warn
items.summary_raw:
Biologists say cargo ships stranded in Gulf may carry highly potent invasive species around the world as trade resumes

  • Middle East crisis – live updates

The closure of the strait of Hormuz has created conditions for an extreme global biodiversity threat, with scientists warning that thousands of stranded ships could spread invasive marine species across the world’s oceans once they begin sailing again.

More than 1,500 commercial vessels have been stuck in the Gulf since the strategic waterway closed on 28 February after the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran. An international team of marine biologists said that with the stranded ships remaining motionless, their hulls were becoming encrusted with marine life – from microbes and algae to barnacles and other invertebrates – that could hitchhike to ports around the world when trade resumed.

items.title: Visioner 🇺🇸🤝🇺🇦 Fox News host Sean Hannity paid an emotional tribute to President Volodymyr Zelensky during the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, highlighting the late senator's un…
items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇸🤝🇺🇦 Fox News host Sean Hannity paid an emotional tribute to President Volodymyr Zelensky during the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, highlighting the late senator's unwavering admiration for Ukraine's leader and people.  Addressing Zelensky, Hannity said:  🗣️ "President Zelensky, I know that Lindsey would have been deeply moved and honored that you made this long journey to be here today."  He noted that Senator Graham passed away shortly after returning from another visit to Kyiv, where he had met with the Ukrainian president.  🗣️ "He saw you, and he said it to me once, as a warrior-poet or a warrior-comedian. He used those terms."  Hannity concluded by recalling Graham's profound respect for Ukraine's resistance.  🗣️ "He was proud of you and the courage of your countrymen."  The remarks underscored the close relationship that developed between Lindsey Graham and Ukraine throughout the war. His repeated visits to Kyiv and steadfast support for Ukraine made him one of the most prominent American political voices backing the country's defense against Russian aggression. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that his meeting with Trump at the White House was "excellent", in video remarks made on Tuesday.

The talks “reflected a complete partnership, bilateral support, and an understanding of the shared goal of ensuring that Iran does not acquire a nuclear weapon”, Netanyahu said.

items.summary_raw:
Water disputes can directly drive conflict, but more often, water scarcity acts as a catalyst — one that, combined with other pressures, raises the risk of conflict. This is nothing new; water has shaped human conflict for millennia. What’s changed is the accumulation of stress, as climate change, population growth, human migration, and the intensive demands of agriculture and industry are converging to strain water systems in ways that threaten to exacerbate instability. items.title: Erdogan says Turkey aims to sign energy cooperation deal with Iraq
items.summary_raw:
Erdogan says Turkey aims to sign energy cooperation deal with Iraq

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said on Tuesday that Turkey aims to sign a comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq as soon as possible, adding that Iraq had offered to provide the country with one million barrels of oil.

This comes after talks between Erdogan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara took place amid concerns about global energy shortages resulting from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Almost 4,000 people evacuated from tourist sites near Bordeaux as wildfires rage in France and Spain
items.summary_raw:
Return of winds and extreme heat threaten firefighters’ attempts to bring blazes under control

Nearly 4,000 people have been evacuated from tourist sites on France’s Atlantic coast as the return of winds and extreme heat jeopardises firefighters’ battles to contain wildfires raging in France and Spain.

The precautionary evacuation order in France, which covers campsites, holiday villages and other tourist accommodation around the resort of Lacanau to the west of Bordeaux, exacerbated a wildfire emergency described by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, as the “toughest” situation the country had dealt with since the second world war.

items.title: It’s time to prosecute climate crimes – with laws that already exist | Aaron Regunberg
items.summary_raw:
Some have called for Nuremberg-style trials against big oil. But there are laws already on the books to describe companies’ conduct

The sky outside is hazy orange, and my five-year-old son is screaming bloody murder. “Sorry, buddy, we have to stay inside,” I say. “It’s not safe to breathe out there.” I had told him we’d be going to the beach today. Something inside me tears a little as I wonder how many promises he’ll see similarly broken in the coming years.

Far too many parents were forced to have some version of this conversation with their children this month, as smoke from record-breaking wildfires poured across the midwest and north-east. Some of them already had to tell their kids that their Fourth of July festivities were canceled because of the lethal heatwave that caused numerous mass casualty events earlier this month.

items.title: Guterres Expresses Strong Commitment to Resolving Cyprus Issue After Meeting with Christodoulides
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres expressed his strong commitment to ensuring that a solution to the Cyprus problem can finally be reached, following his meeting on Tuesday with President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides. “This is a visit of solidarity with the people of Cyprus and to demonstrate my strong commitment to ensuring that we will finally succeed in finding a solution to the Cyprus problem,” Guterres said as he departed the Presidential Palace. “Of course, this depends on the Cypriots themselves, while the guarantor powers also have a role to play, but I will do everything I can to support Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots at this very important moment,” he stressed.

The post Guterres Expresses Strong Commitment to Resolving Cyprus Issue After Meeting with Christodoulides appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: OSINTdefender Axios reports that senior Trump administration officials believe sustained economic pressure may ultimately inflict more damage on Iran than an expanded bombing campa…
items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender Axios reports that senior Trump administration officials believe sustained economic pressure may ultimately inflict more damage on Iran than an expanded bombing campaign, pointing to growing signs of financial strain inside the country.  According to Axios, U.S. officials cite intelligence indicating Iran is struggling to fund proxy forces, facing gasoline shortages, and under increasing financial pressure from sanctions led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Officials argue those economic measures, combined with a U.S. naval blockade, could prove more effective over time than additional airstrikes.  Axios also reports Iran continues to seek sanctions relief and access to frozen assets through indirect talks mediated by Oman, Qatar, and Pakistan, while the Trump administration insists any agreement must also address Tehran's remaining nuclear material. The report notes President Trump's decision to pause strikes followed military concerns over air defense interceptor stockpiles but says officials characterize those warnings as a risk assessment rather than the primary driver of the decision. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz:

We will not allow Erdogan to strengthen Syria against us. We know how to defend Israel's interests.

But Erdogan should also make sure he has no such ambition, because our strength is with us.

items.title: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
items.summary_raw:
From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown

“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan.

The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.”

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ Romanian Ministry of Energy: One of the reactors at the Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant will be temporarily shut down starting July 28 as a precautionary measure due to low water flow in the Danube River. This measure is preventive and necessary to protect equipment associated with three pumps of the cooling system. Any potential malfunction in one of the pumps would require complex repairs lasting several months and could extend up to a year. Peak consumption this week is estimated at approximately 7,300 megawatts, which is about 700 megawatts less than the peak values recorded in previous weeks due to the holiday period. The estimated volume of domestic production will range between 4,000 and 4,300 megawatts, and the difference needed to cover consumption will be provided through imports under commercial terms. • 18:50 — Romanian Ministry of Energy: The difference in quantities required for consumption will be covered without any risks. (Rasd Akhbar Shehaba)

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender RT @HM_Int3lligence: Belgian authorities have arrested a woman who was interning at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) in Mons, Belgium, on suspicion of espionage. The woman, a Canadian citizen of Chinese origin, was detained on Friday, and the Belgian Federal Public Prosecutor's Office announced the arrest on Saturday.  Prosecutors suspect that she was spying for a third country and was a member of a criminal organization. Investigators conducted searches at both her home and her workplace at SHAPE. The investigation began when SHAPE's own security services flagged her conduct and reported their concerns to Belgian military intelligence, which subsequently referred the matter to federal prosecutors.  SHAPE is NATO's primary military command in Europe, led by the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, and plays a central role in the alliance's operational planning. A SHAPE spokesperson stated that there is no indication that NATO's or SHAPE's operational readiness, command and control arrangements, or ongoing tasks have been affected, confirming that the headquarters continues to operate normally. items.title: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot on Iran:  Regarding Iran, there is one supreme objective and two other very important objectives. The supreme objective is to remove the approximately 440 ki…
items.summary_raw: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot on Iran:  Regarding Iran, there is one supreme objective and two other very important objectives. The supreme objective is to remove the approximately 440 kilograms of enriched uranium from Iran.  If that is not done, the Iranians can, by their own decision, break out toward a nuclear weapon. What does that mean?  It means deciding to enrich uranium from 60% to 90%. That would require only about 250–300 centrifuges operating for roughly three weeks, and they could reach weapons-grade enrichment (90%) and shock the world with a nuclear explosive capability.  Therefore, this is the central challenge that Israel must address together with the United States.  Unfortunately, despite notable military achievements, there has not been even one millimeter of progress toward this goal.

items.title: The Guardian view on Europe’s wildfires: politics must catch up with the new reality | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
At a time when the quickening pace of global heating has never been clearer, climate policies are being deprioritised

A new and ominous word has entered the vocabulary of firefighters struggling to cope with the vast wildfire sweeping through south-west France. A pyrocumulonimbus is a fire-generated thunderstorm that can whip up winds in unpredictable ways, making the containment of a blaze and assessment of its likely course far more difficult. A known phenomenon in North America and Australia, firefighters believe France is suffering its first in the Bordeaux region, as the country endures the consequences of the third major heatwave of the summer and prepares for a fourth.

items.title: The AHEPA 104th Supreme Convention Kicked off on July 26
items.summary_raw:
PHILADELPHIA – AHEPA's 104th Supreme Convention celebrating America during its 250th Anniversary kicked off on July 26 in Philadelphia. As AHEPA opened for business, it chose its Founders Day to kick off the epic week ahead. On this date in 1922, eight visionary Greek immigrants came together in a fraternal bond to form the Order of AHEPA in Atlanta, Georgia, to combat discrimination, bigotry, and intolerance; and to help Greek immigrants assimilate into the mainstream of American society with an emphasis on education and philanthropy, fostering American patriotism, and practicing good citizenship. Since that initial gathering 104 years ago, AHEPA has helped countless Greek Americans pursue and fulfill the American Dream.

items.title: Critical Three Days for Cyprus: UN Secretary-General Arrives in Nicosia
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA – The UN Secretary-General is making a new intervention in the Cyprus issue, hoping to break the diplomatic stalemate and restart negotiations aimed at resolving the long-standing conflict. António Guterres is expected to arrive in Nicosia on Monday evening, July 27 and will hold a series of meetings over the following two days. On Tuesday at 10:00 AM local time, Guterres will meet with President Nikos Christodoulides. At 11:45 AM, he will meet Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman in the northern, Turkish-controlled part of Nicosia. That evening, Guterres will host a private dinner with both leaders at the residence of his Special Representative in Cyprus, Hasan Diyan, located near the abandoned Nicosia International Airport in the UN buffer zone.

The post Critical Three Days for Cyprus: UN Secretary-General Arrives in Nicosia appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Why Norway and Finland Should Preserve Two of Europe’s Most Important Security Arrangements

Svalbard is a stark archipelago of glaciers and coal mines lying 650 kilometers (403 miles) north of Norway’s North Cape, roughly halfway between the Norwegian mainland and the North Pole. It belongs to Norway but is governed under a 1920 treaty that grants nationals of more than 40 signatory states sweeping economic rights while barring Oslo from constructing naval bases or using the archipelago for “warlike” purposes. items.title: Pedro Sánchez says Spain is suffering effects of climate crisis as firefighters battle wildfires in France
items.summary_raw:
Blazes near Madrid coming under control but efforts to contain huge fire near Bordeaux hampered by windy conditions

Authorities in France are battling to contain a huge wildfire near Bordeaux in the south-west as Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, warned Spain and the Iberian peninsula were suffering the effects of the climate emergency.

Efforts to extinguish the blaze in the Gironde region of France – which has consumed an area four times the size of Paris and caused nearly 220,000 people to be evacuated – were hampered by windy conditions on Saturday night.

items.summary_raw: Chinese state media, citing top radar scientist Academician Ben De, claims that Pakistani J-10CE fighter jets used their onboard KLJ-7A AESA radars to detect, track, and shoot down Indian jets at ranges near 200 km during the May 2025 clashes, without relying on AWACS or a networked kill chain.  Gallium nitride modules and low-probability-of-intercept waveforms meant Indian Rafales, MiG-29s, and Su-30MKIs allegedly never got a lock warning before PL-15 missiles hit.  US and French officials have confirmed at least one Rafale and one other Indian jet were downed by J-10s that night.  Source: Sohu

items.summary_raw: The US has burned through roughly a third of its total pre-war stockpile of key precision munitions in Iran War.  Interceptors are the most exposed: up to 80% of THAAD (190–290 of 360), more than half of SM-3 (130–250 of 410), and up to 61% of Patriots (1,060–1,430 of 2,330) are gone.  Long-range strike weapons are also depleted at scale, with 1,000+ Tomahawks and 1,100+ JASSMs used, and nearly the entire small PrSM stockpile (40–70 of 90) fired.  Source: ABC, CSIS

items.title: Report: Trump paused Iran escalation over Patriot interceptor concerns
items.summary_raw:
Report: Trump paused Iran escalation over Patriot interceptor concerns

US President Donald Trump has, for now, set aside plans to sharply escalate the American military campaign against Iran, with growing concern that a wider war could dangerously deplete the Pentagon's stockpile of Patriot missile interceptors and other air defence munitions in the Middle East, The New York Times reports.

According to the newspaper, Trump discussed the conflict with senior advisers and cabinet officials during a meeting on Friday.

items.summary_raw:
Temperatures of 95-105F (35-40C) are expected, spanning Gulf of Mexico coast to the Great Plains and the midwest

About 70 million people in the US are set to face excessive heat advisories as dangerously hot temperatures scorch much of the country’s southern and central states.

The third major “heat dome” event to hit the US in the past month is gathering strength over the weekend, spanning a vast swathe of the country, from the Gulf of Mexico coast to the Great Plains and the midwest.

The massive Houthi missile strike on the critical Saudi oil facility triggered raging fires, marking a dramatic escalation following a intense sequence of naval blockades, tanker strikes, and retaliatory Saudi airstrikes on the Yemeni port city of Hodeidah. With Saudi Arabia launching immediate counter-strikes across Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen, both sides are now locked in a dangerous, direct military exchange that threatens to engulf regional energy infrastructure.  This direct strike on Saudi oil assets exposes the ultimate fragility of regional energy security when proxy conflicts bleed into sovereign trade assets. By hitting Aramco, the Houthis are attempting to force a lethal economic toll on Riyadh, proving once again that global oil supplies remain painfully vulnerable to asymmetrical missile warfare despite years of regional containment efforts. items.title: Mitsotakis to Christodoulides: Greece Fully Supports Your Initiatives for Substantive Resumption of Cyprus Talks
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece fully supports the initiatives of Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides for a substantive resumption of talks on the Cyprus issue, during their meeting at the Maximos Mansion in Athens on Saturday. Mitsotakis referred to the wildfires in Spain and France, noting that they once again highlight the importance of the joint Greek-Cypriot initiative to develop a stronger Civil Protection mechanism at European level. He added that Greece is already contributing two firefighting aircraft to efforts to contain the major fires near Madrid.

The post Mitsotakis to Christodoulides: Greece Fully Supports Your Initiatives for Substantive Resumption of Cyprus Talks appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired from Yemen
items.summary_raw:
Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired from Yemen

Saudii Arabia's air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles launched from Yemen, Reuters is reporting.

The missiles were downed by a Greek-operated air defence system and targeted oil refineries in the western city of Yanbu, according to the report.

Earlier, Saudi authorities issued warnings to residents in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu after Yemen's Houthi group vowed to retaliate for attacks carried out by the kingdom this week.

items.summary_raw:
Officials in Spain warn winds could worsen fires on Saturday

  • Tell us: have you been affected by wildfires in Europe?

The French prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, has requested the armed forces to deploy an Airbus A400M military transport aircraft earlier than originally planned to help tackle the major wildfires in Gironde, according to Le Monde.

The French newspaper reported the aircraft’s use was not originally expected until the end of the month due to the technical preparations and tests required beforehand.

While the fires raging across forests in France are a dramatic reminder of three successive heatwaves in as many months, the state of the country’s rivers provides another, no less worrying insight into the impact of extreme heat supercharged by the climate crisis.

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ 🔺Egyptian Foreign Minister's Phone Call with Araghchi and Al-Busaidi 🔹The Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Sameh Shoukry, the country's Foreign Minister, today held two separate phone calls with "Badr Al-Busaidi," the Omani Foreign Minister, and "Sayyed Abbas Araghchi," the Iranian Foreign Minister, to discuss regional developments and recent tensions in vital waterways. 🔹According to a statement from the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Shoukry emphasized in these phone calls the importance of maintaining maritime security and the freedom of navigation for ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, considering it vital for global economic stability and energy security. 🔹The statement added that the Egyptian Foreign Minister also stressed the immediate cessation of all military actions and any tension-inducing activities in the region.

items.summary_raw: Visioner RT @NSTRIKE1231: 🚨🇷🇺⛽️ RUSSIA SUFFERS A MAJOR BLOW AS A KEY BLACK SEA OIL EXPORT TERMINAL HALTS TANKER OPERATIONS.   According to Bloomberg, the Sheskharis oil terminal on Russia’s Black Sea coast has officially stopped receiving tankers since July 21.  Since the beginning of 2026, the terminal had exported an average of 650,000 barrels of oil per day, accounting for roughly one-fifth of Russia’s total oil exports. The suspension therefore represents a significant disruption to one of Moscow’s most important energy export hubs.  The development comes as Russia’s Ministry of Defense officially declared that Russia’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea has become hazardous for navigation due to continuous Ukrainian aerial strikes.  The timing of these events highlights the growing impact of Ukraine’s long-range campaign against Russia’s strategic infrastructure, with attacks increasingly threatening not only military facilities but also the energy and maritime networks that generate billions of dollars in export revenue.  See the latest updates with us: @NSTRIKE1231 tweet

items.title: Morning recap
items.summary_raw:
Morning recap

Good morning, Middle East Eye readers,

The US president, Donald Trump, has said the Iranians are in talks with the United States, and that he is willing to listen, but emphasised that Tehran cannot have a nuclear weapon.

He added that he has not decided on whether to go ahead with the large-scale military campaign he had warned of earlier.

Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has said that “the existing insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and the region is exclusively caused by the US breach of the agreement”.

Israeli forces, meanwhile, raided some 70 homes and arrested around 50 Palestinians overnight in the town of Tal, southwest of Nablus, Al Jazeera reported. The raids have surged amid calls by human rights groups to stop settler "pogroms" in the occupied West Bank.

More than four decades have elapsed since Evangelos Geroliolios made his first ascent to the home of the ancient gods. At the top of Mount Olympus, on the rocky peak of Greece’s highest mountain, he felt unalloyed awe.

“I’ve never forgotten that unique moment, that unique feeling up there on the throne of Zeus,” recalled Geroliolios, who as mayor of Dion-Olympus now spends a great deal of his time administering the area around the site.

Massive operational demands in CENTCOM have forced an unprecedented expenditure of high-end air defense interceptors like Patriot and THAAD, alongside offensive strike weapons like Tomahawk cruise missiles and JASSMs. With defense industrial production lines unable to keep up with the burn rate, U.S. commanders are now actively rationing premier munitions and shifting to lower-cost guided bombs like JDAMs and Small Diameter Bombs to preserve critical inventory.  This dangerous stockpile drain reveals the glaring limitations of the U.S. defense industrial base in sustaining multi-theater strategy. As advanced interceptors disappear into Middle Eastern battlefields faster than factories can build them, Washington faces a high-stakes strategic dilemma—sacrificing long-term Pacific deterrence for immediate regional containment, and exposing a critical vulnerability that global adversaries are watching very closely. Following recent Black Sea naval drone strikes on tankers at the Novorossiysk terminal, Kazakhstan officially froze crude shipments through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium. The sudden export freeze forced a massive 21% collapse in Kazakhstan's national oil output, dropping the giant Tengiz field's production by over half.   Romania, which relies on Kazakh crude for nearly half of its refinery processing, is taking the hardest blow—triggering surging domestic fuel prices, forcing authorities to tap strategic reserves, and threatening vital downstream fuel flows to Moldova and Ukraine. items.title: Less than 24 hours after the US and Saudi Arabia signed a civilian nuclear agreement, Trump effectively put it on hold by adding a new condition: Saudi Arabia must first join the A…
items.summary_raw: Less than 24 hours after the US and Saudi Arabia signed a civilian nuclear agreement, Trump effectively put it on hold by adding a new condition: Saudi Arabia must first join the Abraham Accords and normalize relations with Israel.  The reversal was driven by several factors:  Trump was angry that Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced the deal without informing him first.  The White House viewed the agreement as premature, arguing it was not finalized because required notifications to Congress had not yet been sent.  Conservative backlash quickly mounted. Fox News hosts and a Wall Street Journal editorial criticized the deal for giving Saudi Arabia nuclear cooperation without requiring normalization with Israel—a condition the Biden administration had also pursued.  Trump responded by publicly reinstating that requirement, insisting Saudi Arabia must join the Abraham Accords before the deal can move forward.  Source: CNN

items.title: Trump’s F-35 ‘Consideration’: Reality or Hot Air?
items.summary_raw:
Donald Trump’s suggestion that he might grant Turkey the F-35 has understandably alarmed Greece. Turkish possession of F-35s in numbers larger than Greece can afford would seriously weaken Greece’s capacity to deter its predatory neighbor in the Aegean, Cyprus and the eastern Mediterranean. Greece has long depended on superior technology to offset Turkey’s advantages: more tanks, more aircraft, more ships, seven times the population and an economy roughly five times larger. Turkey has also built a large and efficient arms industry. Small wonder that Greece has consistently spent a larger share of its national wealth on defense than every other European country – until Putin attacked Ukraine – and sometimes more than the United States.

The post Trump’s F-35 ‘Consideration’: Reality or Hot Air? appeared first on The National Herald.

  • Europe live – latest updates

Authorities in south-western France have ordered the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast by land and sea as an “intense and highly unpredictable” wildfire advances on one of the country’s best-known holiday spots.

The fire had burned more than 10,000 hectares (24,700 acres) by Friday morning, the French interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said, with 40,000 people already or about to be evacuated, including thousands of tourists from campsites and rental homes.

items.title: The Guardian view on Britain’s uninhabitable homes: as temperatures rise, a new approach is needed | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
Sadiq Khan’s heat-ready plan for London is a sensible strategy for adaptation that should provide a roadmap for other cities

“Our ability to trust that our homes will keep us safe from the outside is under threat,” the geographer Sam Johnson-Schlee writes in Hot House, his recent book on how heat has transformed domestic life. This summer, high temperatures have become inescapable. People have coped with makeshift solutions: keeping curtains drawn, placing foil over windows or – for those who can afford one – plugging in an air-conditioning unit. Planning experts warn that, with only about half of councils requiring new buildings to include cooling strategies, many homes will become “death traps” as temperatures rise.

Britain’s homes weren’t built to cope with this. The country’s historically mild climate allowed developers to build houses without insulation, while industrialisation supplied plentiful coal to burn
